title: Mixing: Dear Boy by Paul and Linda McCartney | 1971
content:
Studio B, Sound Recorders Studio, Los Angeles
Producer: Paul McCartney
Engineer: Eirik Wangberg

A mixing session for the Ram song ‘Dear Boy’ took place on 14 March 1971.

The album sessions had relocated to Sound Recorders Studio in LA at the beginning of the month, with sessions produced by Jim Guercio and engineered by Armin Steiner. McCartney decided to take back the producer role from Guercio, and Steiner excused himself at the same time.

Steiner appointed Eirik Wangberg in his place. Wangberg – nicknamed ‘the Norwegian’ by McCartney – was Sound Recorders’ in-house engineer, and had a good track record. He went to the studio alone on this day to review the album multitracks.

McCartney was aware of this, and dropped by at around 1pm. He wished to know whether Wangberg was good at mixing, so set him the task of mixing ‘Dear Boy’ within two hours.

It was quite a challenge for me, but when it works, it’s really lots of fun, especially if the arranger knows his job. As Paul really knew what he was doing, the harmonies and voice tracks did not step on each other or kill each other in the mix.
Eirik Wangberg, 26 May 2016
The McCartney Legacy: Volume 1: 1969-73, Allan Kozinn, Adrian Sinclair

McCartney was pleased with the results, so Wangberg remained on the Ram sessions until the end of the project.
